newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds rise, test resistance levels.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds rise, test resistance levels.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished higher Tuesday as the market tested some important resistance levels.
"There was an important rally today," said a trader at a foreign bank.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 hit a high of 92-3/8 during the session, before settling at 92-1/8, up 1/8. Dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 bonds due 2001 rose $0.15 to 126.95.
Traders said the market looked set for further gains but rises depended on the outcome of the awaited Humphrey-Hawkins testimony Wednesday by U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.
"We will have to see what happens tomorrow," said another bond trader.
Market operators said some players booked profits this session but that was not enough to prevent the market from continuing Monday's rise.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.98 percent from 6.13 percent.
